title: Greek Building Blocks
kidRule: Lots of long words are built from little Greek pieces, like building blocks! TELE means far, MICRO means small, SCOPE means look, GRAPH means write, METER means measure, BIO means life, and AUTO means self. Spot the pieces and a long word is easy: MICRO + SCOPE = MICROSCOPE.
hint: This long word is built from Greek pieces. Can you hear a piece you know, like TELE, MICRO, SCOPE, GRAPH, METER, BIO or AUTO? Spell that piece the way it is always spelled.
reminder: Spell the Greek piece the same way every time: T-E-L-E, M-I-C-R-O, S-C-O-P-E, G-R-A-P-H, M-E-T-E-R, B-I-O, A-U-T-O.

check.question: Why is MICROSCOPE spelled M-I-C-R-O and then S-C-O-P-E?
check.correctAnswer: It is built from two Greek pieces: MICRO for small and SCOPE for look!
distractors: Because every science word must have two letter Cs
Because long words always use the letter C and never the letter K

words.def: A machine you use to talk with someone who is far away.
words.sent: Grandma called us on the telephone.
words.story: Tele means far and phone means sound, so this word means 'far sound'. Alexander Graham Bell made the first telephone call in 1876!
words.card: Only *one* banana at a time may talk on the *telephone*!

words.def: A tool that makes very tiny things look big enough to see.
words.sent: We looked at a drop of pond water under the microscope.
words.story: Micro means small and scope means look, so a microscope is a 'small-looker'. With one you can see the tiny cells in the skin of an onion!
words.card: The *cop* used a *microscope* to find out who took the cookie crumbs!

words.def: A group of sentences that are all about one idea.
words.sent: I wrote a paragraph about my pet turtle.
words.story: Graph means write. Long ago, a paragraph was a little mark written in the margin of a page to show where a new idea began!
words.card: The pirate wrote a whole *paragraph* on an old *rag* because he ran out of paper!

words.def: A person's own name, written by that person.
words.sent: The soccer star wrote her autograph on my ball.
words.story: Auto means self and graph means write, so an autograph is something you write yourself: your very own name!
words.card: The famous giraffe signed an *autograph* on my *graph* paper with its tongue!

words.def: A length used for measuring long distances, a bit more than half a mile.
words.sent: The park is one kilometer from our house.
words.story: Kilo means a thousand and meter means measure, so a kilometer is exactly 1,000 meters long!
words.card: The snail ran a whole *kilometer* carrying a *kilo* of jellybeans!

words.def: The science of living things, like plants, animals, and people.
words.sent: In biology we learned how a tadpole turns into a frog.
words.story: Bio means life and the ending -logy means 'the study of', so biology is the study of life!
words.card: The frog sat on a *log* and read a *biology* book all about itself!

words.def: Working by itself, without a person doing each step.
words.sent: The automatic door slid open as we walked up.
words.story: Auto means self, so an automatic machine does its job by itself. Your heart is automatic too: it beats without you having to think about it!
words.card: The *automatic* door opened for the cat on the *mat*, again and again and again!

words.def: A tube with mirrors inside that lets you see over or around things.
words.sent: The submarine captain looked through the periscope.
words.story: Peri means around and scope means look. A periscope uses two mirrors to bend the light, so sailors under the water can see what is above it!
words.card: How does a nosy submarine *cope*? It pokes up its *periscope*!

words.def: A tool that measures how hot or cold something is.
words.sent: The thermometer showed that it was freezing outside.
words.story: Thermo means heat and meter means measure, so a thermometer is a heat-measurer!
words.card: *Mom* gave the snowman a *thermometer* to see if he had a cold!

words.def: A tube you look into and turn to see colorful, changing patterns.
words.sent: I turned the kaleidoscope and the colors danced.
words.story: A Scottish scientist named David Brewster invented the kaleidoscope around 1816. He built its name from Greek words meaning 'beautiful shape to look at'!
words.card: I wore a flower *lei* and saw a hundred of them in my *kaleidoscope*!
